Jake / Tessa —

Quick triage notes after looking at the VectorPay traces you sent:
- We see repeated "chunk-silence" coincident with periods of high batch fan-in (many concurrent short-lived calls).
- No HTTP 5xxs at the API gateway; our edge shows continuous connections, but the worker host logs show an intermittent 30–200ms stall in the token-emit loop that cascades when several requests align.
- Hypothesis: autoscaler/pool-reassignment + a temporary KV-cache eviction under memory pressure. When a worker regains KV state it emits buffered tokens in a burst; the client sees a lull followed by a spike.

Action I'm taking now:
1) Pinned the VectorPay traffic to a warm pool to eliminate pool reassignment variance.
2) Increasing K/V cache retention for the next 2 hours for their tenant.
3) Enabling more verbose token-emitter tracing; will push logs to the shared Drive link.

I'll follow up in 30m with logs and a proposed mitigation. If this recurs post-mitigation we'll escalate to infra to check for CPU scheduling anomalies.

- Marcus

Jake / team —

Follow-up from infra review overnight: we observed a correlated bump in kernel-level context switches and a small but measurable increase in GC pause tail latency on nodes serving VectorPay during the peak window. Two factors appear to align to cause the symptom you described:

1) Batching burst pattern: many short-lived generator contexts allocate small ephemeral buffers and cause GC churn; combined with short-lived GRPC streams, the runtime enters a backpressure oscillation where token emission is delayed.
2) Proxy read buffer coalescing: certain upstream proxies (including a subset of our edge binary instances) attempt to coalesce small writes and pause flushing until a threshold; when combined with the above stalls, client sockets observe silence.

Mitigation plan enacted: 
- We deployed a hotfix to change emitter scheduling (reduce synchronous GC allocations during heavy fan-in) and disabled write coalescing on the affected edge pool.
- We increased the per-tenant warm pool size temporarily and added a circuit-breaker threshold that will fail fast (500) rather than silently stall if token emission exceeds X ms for Y requests — this makes the failure visible to clients.

Expected impact: should reduce silent-chunk windows to under 1s for the next 24–48h while we validate. Rollback: revert the emitter scheduling change and re-enable coalescing (we have immediate rollback runbooks).

I'll post detailed traces and the changed runtime flags to the Drive link shortly.

— Neha
Head of Reliability Engineering
